dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Hello, I'm Ishizu.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Welcome to Harie.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Here, water is always right beside you in daily life.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: I've been hearing the sound of water ever since I arrived.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: I think you'll understand better once you walk around.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: First, please go take a look at the rice fields.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Understood. I'll take a look around.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Have you seen the rice field?

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Yes. The water was colder than I expected.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: It takes a little time for the seedlings to get used to the cold.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: So the seedlings need to adjust to the water.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Yes. That time is also part of growing rice.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: You'll understand even more if you look at the other work going on.

updateNotebook.memo: It takes time for seedlings to adjust to the cold.
updateNotebook.quote: That time is also part of growing rice.
updateNotebook.speaker: ishizu

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Have you seen the weeding too?

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Yes. Everyone was working quietly and diligently.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: It's steady work, but it's essential to growing rice.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: You do it by hand, not with machines?

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: The weeds near the water have to be pulled by hand to get them out by the roots.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: You'll come to understand the relationship between water and grass as you keep observing.

updateNotebook.memo: Weeds near the water must be pulled by hand to remove them completely.
updateNotebook.quote: You'll come to understand the relationship between water and grass as you keep observing.
updateNotebook.speaker: ishizu

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Did you see the potato sorting too?

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Yes. They were separating the big ones from the small ones.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: That's a daily task here in Harie.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Everyone was very skilled at it.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Do it long enough, and it comes naturally.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Sorting the harvest is also part of daily life.

updateNotebook.memo: Sorting the harvest is part of daily life.
updateNotebook.quote: Do it long enough, and it comes naturally.
updateNotebook.speaker: ishizu

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Take your time looking around today.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Looks like you've been walking quite a bit.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Yes. After talking to so many people, I've gotten hungry.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: In that case, you should head over to the inn.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: There's rice cooked with Harie's water and warm dishes waiting.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: Food made with Harie's water... I'm curious.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: First, take a look around outside the inn.

setStoryHint.text: Let's take a look around the inn.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: I saw water being used in so many parts of daily life inside the inn.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: That's right. Cooking, bathing—in Harie, everything goes hand in hand with water.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Next, you should visit the community center. You'll see how the villagers are connected.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: I'd like to know more about Harie's future.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: There are still places you haven't seen. Feel free to walk around the village.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: You've been all around the village, then.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text:
Yes. The water, the festival, the empty houses...
I also learned that the Okawa River flows all the way to Lake Biwa.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: Here in Harie, water connects everything.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text: If we don't create ways to make a living, the young ones won't come back.

dialogs.speaker: machi
dialogs.text: But the water keeps flowing, doesn't it.

dialogs.speaker: ishizu
dialogs.text:
That's right. As long as the water lives, Harie won't disappear.
The answer is in the water.
